title: Scout C4 (web + local): running Claude Code and Codex CLIs headless on a Linux server with Max and ChatGPT subscriptions — supported auth paths and terms
spec: Web-and-local scout. Question: how can `claude -p` (Claude Code CLI, Max subscription, two profiles via CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) and `codex exec` (Codex CLI, ChatGPT plan) run unattended on a headless Ubuntu 20.04 server that the user owns, without copying browser sessions around. Use WebSearch/WebFetch on docs.anthropic.com / code.claude.com (Claude Code: `claude setup-token`, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, headless mode, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, whether subscription OAuth may be used in automation and any stated limits), and on the Codex CLI docs/GitHub (openai/codex: `codex login` device or headless flow, CODEX_HOME, auth.json portability, ChatGPT-plan use in non-interactive runs). Also run locally: `claude --version`, `claude --help | head -60`, `codex --version`, `codex login --help` (do not log in or out). Report: (1) the supported non-interactive auth path for each CLI with the doc URL; (2) whether credentials created on one machine may be moved to another per the docs; (3) Ubuntu 20.04 compatibility (glibc, node version) for each CLI; (4) anything in the terms that limits automation on a subscription plan. Mark every web finding provenance web and quote the doc sentence. Do not change any login state.
acceptance: Result names a supported headless auth path for each CLI with a doc URL and quote
Result states installed versions locally and Ubuntu 20.04 compatibility findings
Result flags any terms-of-use constraint on automated subscription use

findings.claim: Claude Code's supported non-interactive auth path is `claude setup-token`, which mints a one-year OAuth token you export as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN; this is documented as the intended path for CI/scripts on a Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise plan.
provenance: web:https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication — quote: "For CI pipelines, scripts, or other environments where interactive browser login isn't available, generate a one-year OAuth token with `claude setup-token`... It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN environment variable wherever you want to authenticate... This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan."

findings.claim: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN only works in normal (non-bare) mode; `--bare` mode never reads OAuth/keychain credentials and needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper instead — relevant since headless scripts are pushed toward --bare.
provenance: web:https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication — quote: "Bare mode does not read CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. If your script passes --bare, authenticate with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an apiKeyHelper instead."

findings.claim: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR relocates the credentials file (and the macOS Keychain lookup key) so two profiles pointed at two different CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR values keep separate logins/tokens on the same machine — this is the documented mechanism for the user's two-profile setup.
provenance: web:https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication — quote: "If you've set the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR environment variable, Claude Code keeps the .credentials.json file under that directory instead... and keys the macOS Keychain entry to that directory too, so a session with a different CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR reads a different entry."

findings.claim: Claude Code officially supports Ubuntu 20.04+ (native install), with Node.js only required (v22+) if installing via npm; the native/apt binary does not run on the host Node runtime at all.
provenance: web:https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup — quote: "Ubuntu 20.04+" under Operating system; and "the npm package requires Node.js 22 or later... the package downloads a native binary that doesn't use your Node.js at runtime"

findings.claim: Locally installed versions: claude 2.1.276, codex-cli 0.154.0, local node v26.0.0 (macOS scout machine — not the target Ubuntu 20.04 server, so this node version is not evidence of server compatibility).

Codex CLI's documented non-interactive/headless auth path is `codex login --device-auth` (device-code flow, confirmed present as a flag in local `codex login --help`), producing ~/.codex/auth.json under CODEX_HOME; `codex exec` reuses whatever credentials are already in CODEX_HOME.
evidence: local shell: codex login --help → shows `--device-auth` flag
provenance: web:https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth — quote: "In the interactive login UI, select Sign in with Device Code" (device-code / headless flow for remote environments without browser access)

open_questions: No primary-source (openai/codex repo or learn.chatgpt.com) page was fetched that states an explicit minimum glibc/Ubuntu version for the Codex CLI Rust binary — only secondary blogs were found, and they conflict internally (glibc 2.39+ vs Ubuntu 20.04+ support). Should verify against the actual release asset names/checksums on https://github.com/openai/codex/releases.

Anthropic's Consumer Terms of Service and Usage Policy pages (anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms, anthropic.com/legal/aup) were not fetched directly — findings on 'ordinary, individual usage' and third-party restrictions are sourced from the code.claude.com legal-and-compliance page, which links to but paraphrases those terms.

Did not test whether `claude setup-token` or `codex login --device-auth` can complete without a browser at all on a truly headless box (e.g., copy-paste code flow) — only documented flag/env-var existence was confirmed, not an actual headless login (login state was not changed, per task constraints).
suggested_next: Have a human run `claude setup-token` and `codex login --device-auth` interactively once (accepting the browser/device-code prompt) on the target Ubuntu 20.04 box or a trusted machine, capture the resulting CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and ~/.codex/auth.json, and verify `claude -p` / `codex exec` work non-interactively from those.

Fetch https://github.com/openai/codex/releases directly (not via search snippets) to confirm the actual Linux asset names and whether a musl build is offered, to settle the Ubuntu 20.04/glibc question with a primary source.

Read Anthropic's Consumer Terms of Service and Usage Policy pages directly for the authoritative 'ordinary use' / automation language, since this scout only read Anthropic's paraphrase on code.claude.com.
